blocks.prompt: 10 How many committees of 5 members can be chosen from a group of 8 persons when each committee must include 2 particular persons?
blocks.explanation:
A committee is a selection with a condition: 2 particular persons are always in it.
We must count the committees.
Plan: put the 2 persons in first, then choose the remaining \(5 - 2 = 3\) members from the remaining \(8 - 2 = 6\) persons.
steps:
Given: 8 persons; committee of 5; 2 particular persons must be included.
To find: the number of such committees.
Method: Fixed members need no choice (1 way). Only the free places are filled, by \({}^{n}C_{r}\).

Fix the 2 particular persons
\[\text{places left} = 5 - 2 = 3\]
\[\text{persons left} = 8 - 2 = 6\]
Why: The 2 persons are already in, so they can neither be chosen again nor left out.

Choose the other 3 members
\[{}^{6}C_{3} = \dfrac{6 \cdot 5 \cdot 4}{3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{120}{6} = 20\]
Why: 3 places from 6 persons, order not important.

Check by counting the opposite way
\[{}^{8}C_{5} = 56 \text{ committees in all}\]
\[\text{with both: } 20,\ \text{at most one: } 36\]
\[\text{at most one} = {}^{6}C_{5} + 2 \cdot {}^{6}C_{4} = 6 + 30 = 36 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Committees with neither of the two (\({}^{6}C_{5}\)) or with exactly one (\(2 \times {}^{6}C_{4}\)) make up the rest of the 56.
